correctness.rationale: Exact factorization gives pairwise gcd control; integrality restricts all odd denominator primes to the other support prime; higher binary bits therefore occur at most once per odd-prime exponent. The sole possible four-component odd case contradicts multiplicative-order divisibility modulo q versus q+1 being a power of two. The published J<=3 classification then yields exactly 6 and 45. Exact bounded replay independently finds only those two examples.

evidence: The 2026 paper gives explicit bounds for arbitrary J and a complete list only for J<=3.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General finiteness and upper bounds do not imply the support-specific collapse J<=3. The new gcd/order argument excludes all unbounded higher-component layers simultaneously.

value.rationale: The number of prime factors is a natural structural invariant for harmonic-number classes. Closing the complete two-prime-support stratum removes all arbitrarily large exponent patterns at once and converts an unbounded classification problem to a known finite low-I-component classification; this is substantially stronger than another bounded enumeration.
